name: Evey Events
summary: Sell event tickets straight from your Shopify store: unlimited events and ticket types, QR check-in, attendee data at checkout.
best_for: Shopify stores that sell tickets alongside products and want attendees, orders and customer data in one place instead of reconciling a separate ticketing platform against the shop
skip_if: ticketing is your actual business rather than a sideline -- a dedicated platform gives you seating, promoter tools and box-office features that a Shopify app is not trying to match -- or you sell so few tickets that any per-ticket fee is friction you don't need
honest_knock: Nobody gets caught by the monthly fee here; they get caught by the per-ticket one. On Lite the app is free to install and then takes a dollar off every ticket you sell, which is invisible until you sell volume and then is the largest line on the invoice. Work out your monthly ticket count before you install anything, because that single number picks your plan: under 76 stay on Lite, 76 to 120 move to Growth, 120 to 560 move to Standard, above that Professional. Getting this wrong is not a small error -- at 300 tickets a month the gap between the best and worst choice is about $65 every month.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Growth · Growth $19 a month plus $0.75 per ticket
pricing.notes: (re-verified 26 November 2026 on apps.shopify.com/event-tickets; every rate unchanged since 1 September 2026) Four tiers, and every one of them charges twice: a monthly fee and a fee per ticket processed. Lite is free to install and takes $1.00 per ticket. Growth is $19 a month and $0.75. Standard, the tier the store marks Popular, is $49 and $0.50. Professional is $189 and $0.25. The paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial. Read that structure the right way round: the monthly fee is not what you are buying, it is what you pay to lower the per-ticket rate, so the correct plan follows from your ticket volume and nothing else. The crossings are exact. Lite and Growth cost the same at 76 tickets a month; below that Lite wins. Growth and Standard cross at 120. Standard and Professional cross at 560. So a store selling 300 tickets a month pays $199 on Standard against $244 on Growth and $264 on Professional -- the middle tier, and the store's own Popular label happens to be right for that range. One feature line changes that arithmetic and sits above the crossover: Collect fees on every ticket sold appears on Standard and Professional only, so passing the per-ticket cost to attendees is itself a paid feature. Beyond that, feature differences barely enter into it until Professional, which is where reserved seating, Klaviyo and Mailchimp integrations, the multi-vendor dashboard and priority support live. The app is published by Staytuned and carries a 4.5 rating from 327 reviews (read 1 October 2026).

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Evey Events & Tickets on a Shopify development store: the install, a recurring event with one saved date in the trial, the plan page, the Shopify approval screen for Lite (a payment method was asked, nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no theme change was saved. Install: the install form was submitted in our own tab at about 15:46 (Mac clock). The Install app dialog said that the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked and the app opened on Events at about 15:47. No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. After the install the app showed two notices: Turn on Evey in your theme by October 1, 2026 and Select a plan when you're ready to launch with Your free trial expires in 7 days; no plan was chosen and the app worked at once in the trial. Core action, a recurring event: Create event, the name Harbour Tour Test, Recurring event and Save Event gave the message Event successfully created at about 15:47 (two steps after filling in the form). The event settings said Storefront product page scheduler is disabled: the storefront integration that adds a button to the product page asking customers to select an event date and time is disabled, and it has to be enabled for a recurring event with multiple dates and times. In the calendar a double click on 24 November opened the dialog Event recurring frequency with Don't repeat. The dropdown for the frequency did not respond to a click or the keyboard (a limit of our test tool in a cross-origin iframe), so no weekly repeat was made; only a single date, 24 November 2026 from 15:00 to 16:00, was saved (Schedule saved, at about 15:48). About 2 minutes passed from the app opening to a saved schedule in the admin. The storefront preview was not opened, the scheduler stayed disabled and the theme embed Turn on Evey was not switched on, so no theme change was saved and no booking was tried. Plans in the app (Change plan): Lite $0 / month plus $1.0 per ticket processed, with Recurring events struck through and also struck through Mailchimp and Klaviyo integrations, Attendee messages & scheduled reminders, Ability to pass ticket fees onto customers, Reserved seating and Shopify Flow integration; Growth $19 / month plus $0.75 per ticket processed; Standard $49 / month plus $0.5 per ticket processed; Professional $189 / month plus $0.25 per ticket processed. The paid plans show 7 trial days remaining. This agrees with the App Store listing. Checkout: choosing Lite opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: Evey Events & Tickets by Staytuned, This app bills you for usage charges, the plan Lite, App spending limit: you'll be charged based on how you use this app, to a maximum of $50.000,00 USD per 30 days, which can be updated after approval, an Add payment method row, and on the right a text that you will be billed for the app when you begin to use it, on your monthly invoice and your threshold bills, with the Approve button greyed out. The sentence You will not be billed for this test charge was not on the screen and a payment method was needed, so nothing was approved: we left the screen with Cancel. The dossier says that the free Lite plan is free to install; the approval screen nevertheless asked for a payment method for it. No card was entered. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app (Open app, View details, Get support, Uninstall); the dialog Uninstall Evey Events & Tickets? says that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. The Uninstall button became active only after a reason was chosen (Testing multiple apps). Not tested: a weekly repeating schedule (the frequency dropdown did not respond), booking in the webshop, scanning and check-in with several scanners, Apple Wallet, emails, payouts and ticket counting. Whether the admin of a real Lite plan behaves like the trial was not tested, because the plan was not approved. Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps at about 15:5x and the installed list no longer showed it; the test event Harbour Tour Test goes with the app; all our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The approval screen for the free Lite plan asked for a payment method and showed a usage charge limit of $50.000,00 USD per 30 days with a greyed out Approve button, the storefront scheduler is disabled until it is switched on, the frequency dropdown did not respond in our tool, and the Lite plan card strikes through recurring events.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Evey Events & Tickets on a Shopify development store: the install, a recurring event with one saved date in the trial, the plan page, the Shopify approval screen for Lite (a payment method was asked, nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no theme change was saved. Install: the install form was submitted in our own tab at about 15:46 (Mac clock). The Install app dialog said that the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. Install was clicked and the app opened on Events at about 15:47. No vendor account, call, demo or phone number was asked. After the install the app showed two notices: Turn on Evey in your theme by October 1, 2026 and Select a plan when you're ready to launch with Your free trial expires in 7 days; no plan was chosen and the app worked at once in the trial. Core action, a recurring event: Create event, the name Harbour Tour Test, Recurring event and Save Event gave the message Event successfully created at about 15:47 (two steps after filling in the form). The event settings said Storefront product page scheduler is disabled: the storefront integration that adds a button to the product page asking customers to select an event date and time is disabled, and it has to be enabled for a recurring event with multiple dates and times. In the calendar a double click on 24 November opened the dialog Event recurring frequency with Don't repeat. The dropdown for the frequency did not respond to a click or the keyboard (a limit of our test tool in a cross-origin iframe), so no weekly repeat was made; only a single date, 24 November 2026 from 15:00 to 16:00, was saved (Schedule saved, at about 15:48). About 2 minutes passed from the app opening to a saved schedule in the admin. The storefront preview was not opened, the scheduler stayed disabled and the theme embed Turn on Evey was not switched on, so no theme change was saved and no booking was tried. Plans in the app (Change plan): Lite $0 / month plus $1.0 per ticket processed, with Recurring events struck through and also struck through Mailchimp and Klaviyo integrations, Attendee messages & scheduled reminders, Ability to pass ticket fees onto customers, Reserved seating and Shopify Flow integration; Growth $19 / month plus $0.75 per ticket processed; Standard $49 / month plus $0.5 per ticket processed; Professional $189 / month plus $0.25 per ticket processed. The paid plans show 7 trial days remaining. This agrees with the App Store listing. Checkout: choosing Lite opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: Evey Events & Tickets by Staytuned, This app bills you for usage charges, the plan Lite, App spending limit: you'll be charged based on how you use this app, to a maximum of $50.000,00 USD per 30 days, which can be updated after approval, an Add payment method row, and on the right a text that you will be billed for the app when you begin to use it, on your monthly invoice and your threshold bills, with the Approve button greyed out. The sentence You will not be billed for this test charge was not on the screen and a payment method was needed, so nothing was approved: we left the screen with Cancel. The dossier says that the free Lite plan is free to install; the approval screen nevertheless asked for a payment method for it. No card was entered. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app (Open app, View details, Get support, Uninstall); the dialog Uninstall Evey Events & Tickets? says that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. The Uninstall button became active only after a reason was chosen (Testing multiple apps). Not tested: a weekly repeating schedule (the frequency dropdown did not respond), booking in the webshop, scanning and check-in with several scanners, Apple Wallet, emails, payouts and ticket counting. Whether the admin of a real Lite plan behaves like the trial was not tested, because the plan was not approved. Clean up: the app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps at about 15:5x and the installed list no longer showed it; the test event Harbour Tour Test goes with the app; all our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The approval screen for the free Lite plan asked for a payment method and showed a usage charge limit of $50.000,00 USD per 30 days with a greyed out Approve button, the storefront scheduler is disabled until it is switched on, the frequency dropdown did not respond in our tool, and the Lite plan card strikes through recurring events.
